study type: Experimental animal study (randomized controlled trial design)
exposure: Airway liquid volumes (simulating vaginal delivery vs. elective cesarean section)
cohort: Surgically instrumented near-term lambs (139 ± 2 days gestational age) randomized into Control or Elevated Liquid groups.
finding: The application of external thoracic pressures significantly influences respiratory function after birth in near-term lambs, with negative pressures improving and positive pressures impairing pulmonary gas exchange.
mod_finding: Lambs with elevated airway liquid, simulating elective cesarean section, showed a greater improvement in pulmonary oxygen exchange (larger reduction in AaDO2) when external negative pressure was applied compared to control lambs simulating vaginal delivery.
followup_time: Observations taken acutely for approximately 1 hour after birth.
